LevelNames.name: Level names, OW border, OW map setup
summary: Overworld data followed by the routines that use it. Parts, in order:
$04A0FC: level name codes, one 16-bit word per level number ($7E:D000 map value, $00-$5C, then $FFFF padding up to $04A3FF).
Probably: high byte (bits 0-6) = index into DATA_049C91 for the first name word, low byte high/low nibbles = DATA_049CCF / DATA_049CED entries.
$04A400: stripe image #6 (overworld border; see ImagePointers) in LoadScrnImage record format, ends with $FF at $04A532.
$04A533: RLE-compressed overworld tilemaps: tile number bytes ($04A533-$04C02A) then tile property bytes ($04C02B-$04D677), each
decoded by CODE_04DABA to every other byte of $7F:4000 (header bit 7 clear: n+1 literal bytes, set: one byte repeated n+1 times).
$04D678: per-level byte table copied to $7E:D800 by CODE_04D7F2 (index = level number, entry 0 unused).
$04D6E9 (long call, from $00:A165 during overworld load): renders the overworld layer 1 tilemap row by row with the level renderer,
then DMAs the decompressed map from $7F:4000 (submap: $7F:6000) to VRAM $3000. Quirk: the submap flag is [$1F11 + player].
$04D770: stores A at index X in 31 tables of $1B0 bytes each starting at $7F:C800 (strides of $1B0), then X++.
$04D7F2: builds the level number map $7E:D000 (each tile $56-$80 of $7E:C800 gets the next number, from 1) and the byte table $7E:D800,
then calls CODE_04DA49 for every level $00-$6E so beaten levels show their cleared tiles.

lines.04A0FC: Levels $00-$03: name code per level (see section summary)
lines.04A1B4: Level $5C name code, then $FFFF padding (unused level numbers)
lines.04A400: VRAM $5000 RLE 319B (record: addr hi/lo, flags+length, data; ends at $FF)
lines.04A530: End of stripe image ($FF at $A532); $A533: start of compressed tile number stream
lines.04C028: End of tile number stream ($C02B: start of compressed tile property stream)
lines.04D678: Levels $00-$07: byte copied to $7E:D800 (index 0 unused; probably path direction bits)
lines.04D6F0: } [$4D] = [$4F] = $FFFF (probably invalidates the cached layer 1 update positions)
lines.04D705: / A = submap the player is on ([$1F11+X] & $0F, 0 = main map)
lines.04D708: On the main map: keep Y position 0
lines.04D70D: / [$47] = $20 (starting value of the row counter for the submap)
lines.04D712: / Layer 1 Y position = $0200 (submap tiles start at row $200)
lines.04D714: Build the layer 1 tilemap row for position [$1C] with the level renderer (CODE_05881A)
lines.04D718: Upload the pending layer 1 tilemap update to VRAM (CODE_0087AD)
lines.04D723: } Layer 1 Y position += $10 (next row of map16 blocks)
lines.04D72B: / Loop until the Y position wraps to a multiple of $200 (32 rows)
lines.04D743: / VMAIN = $80: VRAM address increments after high-byte writes
lines.04D757: } Copy DMA setup from DATA_04DAB3 to $4310-$4316: $7F:4000 to VRAM, $2000 bytes
lines.04D760: A = submap the player is on
lines.04D76C: / Start DMA channel 1: copy the decompressed map to VRAM $3000
lines.04D7F4: A = 0 (B stays 0, so the later TAX is clean)
lines.04D801: } [$0D] = $7E:D000 (24-bit pointer to the level number map)
lines.04D80D: } [$0A] = $7E:D800 (24-bit pointer to the per-level byte table)
lines.04D819: } [$04] = $7E:C800 (24-bit pointer to the overworld layer 1 tile numbers)
lines.04D820: / [$00] = 1: first level number to hand out
lines.04D822: Y = $07FF: clear $800 bytes of each map
lines.04D827: Clear byte Y of the per-level byte table ($7E:D800)
lines.04D829: Clear byte Y of the level number map ($7E:D000)
lines.04D832: A = layer 1 tile number at map position Y
lines.04D836: / Tile < $56: not a level tile, skip
lines.04D83A: / Tile >= $81: not a level tile, skip
lines.04D851: If level [$0F] is beaten, update its map tiles (CODE_04DA49)
